questions.corrige_markdown: **Pollution** is the **contamination (addition) of the environment (air, water or soil) by harmful substances, called pollutants, or by energy (heat, noise), usually as a result of human activities**, in amounts that **harm living organisms** or damage the environment and make it less fit for use.

questions.enonce_markdown:
State two effects each of the following pollutants:

(i) Carbon monoxide

(ii) Chlorofluorocarbons

(iii) Sulphur dioxide

(iv) Smoke

(v) Nitrogen dioxide. *(2, 2, 2, 2, 2 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Carbon monoxide**: (1) combines irreversibly with **haemoglobin** to form carboxyhaemoglobin, so the blood carries less oxygen, causing **headache, dizziness, unconsciousness and death**; (2) reduces the oxygen supply to the foetus and heart (heart disease).

(ii) **Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs)**: (1) **destroy the ozone layer**, which lets more **ultraviolet radiation** reach the earth; (2) the UV causes **skin cancer, cataracts** and damage to crops and plankton; they are also **greenhouse gases** that contribute to global warming.

(iii) **Sulphur dioxide**: (1) dissolves in rain to form **acid rain**, which damages plants, buildings and kills aquatic organisms by acidifying lakes; (2) irritates the eyes and the respiratory tract, causing **bronchitis, asthma and coughing**.

(iv) **Smoke**: (1) causes **respiratory diseases** (bronchitis, lung cancer, asthma); (2) **reduces visibility** and light for photosynthesis, and **blackens buildings** and leaves (soot blocks the stomata).

(v) **Nitrogen dioxide**: (1) forms **acid rain** (nitric acid); (2) irritates the lungs, causing **respiratory problems**, and contributes to **smog** and to the damage of plant leaves.

The **carbon cycle** is the continuous circulation of carbon between the atmosphere (as carbon dioxide) and living organisms.

- **Removal of carbon dioxide from the air**: green plants and algae take in $\mathrm{CO_2}$ and use it in **photosynthesis** to make carbohydrates (glucose, starch), which are later converted to fats and proteins. Carbon is now in the **producers**.
- **Passage along food chains**: herbivores **feed** on plants, and carnivores feed on herbivores, so the carbon compounds pass to **consumers**.
- **Return of carbon dioxide to the air**:
  - **Respiration** of plants, animals and microorganisms releases $\mathrm{CO_2}$.
  - **Decay**: when plants and animals die, and from faeces, **decomposers (bacteria and fungi)** break down the dead matter and release $\mathrm{CO_2}$ by respiration.
  - **Combustion** of wood and **fossil fuels** (coal, oil, gas), formed from remains of dead organisms over millions of years, releases $\mathrm{CO_2}$.
- Carbon dioxide also dissolves in water of oceans and lakes, from which it is used by aquatic plants.

In summary: atmospheric $\mathrm{CO_2}$ $\xrightarrow{\text{photosynthesis}}$ plants $\xrightarrow{\text{feeding}}$ animals $\xrightarrow{\text{respiration, decay, combustion}}$ atmospheric $\mathrm{CO_2}$.

(A labelled flow diagram may be drawn: atmosphere, green plants, animals, dead organisms, decomposers, fossil fuels, with arrows labelled photosynthesis, feeding, respiration, decay and combustion.)
